articles.headline: Yankees predicted to replace Jazz Chisholm with $24M two-time All-Star, Gold Glove finalist
keyFacts: Free agent second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. experienced a difficult 2025 season and postseason with the New York Yankees, but he expressed a desire to return to the team.
Analyst Zach Buckley predicted that the Yankees will sign Brandon Lowe instead of re-signing Chisholm for the upcoming season.
Brandon Lowe finished the final year of a $24 million contract and is a two-time All-Star and Gold Glove finalist.
body: The New York Yankees will have several decisions to make this offseason, and one of the most notable involves Jazz Chisholm Jr. The second baseman is expected to hit free agency and could either return to New York or leave for another team.
Chisholm did not play much during the playoffs, which could lead to frustration. However, he does want to return.

“Chisholm, an All-Star for the second time in 2025, endured a down year at the plate and struggled both offensively and defensively in four appearances in the playoffs. Manager Aaron Boone left Chisholm out of the Yankees' starting lineup for two postseason games, including their season-ending loss on Wednesday. The fans at Yankee Stadium booed Chisholm after he fouled out to first base as a pinch hitter in the bottom of the seventh inning. Nevertheless, Chisholm would rather continue his career with the Yankees than exit in free agency," MLB Trade Rumors' Connor Byrne wrote.
When Chisholm played for the Miami Marlins, Yankees legend Derek Jeter reportedly had to speak with him about staying focused.

“When Jazz was in Miami, Derek Jeter was there as the owner and Don Mattingly was the manager. That's two great Yankees who understood tradition and played the game right. They both met with Chisholm on repeated occasions and begged him to get his head straight,” NJ.com’s Bob Klapisch wrote.
It is difficult to know what will happen this offseason. Bleacher Report’s Zach Buckley believes New York will sign Brandon Lowe instead of bringing back Chisholm.

“Maybe the Pirates' 82 wins, their most since 2018, will embolden them to spend, though Lowe's contract could feature both a big annual salary and a good amount of years. That combination might be more than Pittsburgh's front office can stomach, which would be music to the ears of a certain major-market big-spender with question marks at Lowe's second base position. Prediction: Lowe signs with the New York Yankees,” Buckley wrote.
Lowe could be a suitable replacement, as he has been more consistent at the plate than Chisholm. He also tends to be less vocal when dissatisfied, potentially making him a good fit for the team.
Lowe just finished the final year of his $24 million contract. He is also a solid defender who has been a finalist for a Gold Glove Award. The Yankees could gain a lot by signing Lowe this offseason.

articles.headline: College football player Tyler Ulrich dies five days after ‘traumatic injury’ during game
keyFacts: Southern Nazarene University announced that 21-year-old sophomore safety Tyler Ulrich died five days after sustaining a traumatic injury during a football game.
School officials did not reveal the specific cause of death or the nature of the injury Ulrich suffered during Saturday's game against Ouachita Baptist.
Southern Nazarene University announced that they have canceled their upcoming football game against Southwestern Oklahoma State scheduled for Saturday.
body: Southern Nazarene University in Oklahoma announced on Thursday that sophomore safety Tyler Ulrich has died five days after sustaining what the school called a “traumatic injury” during a game against Ouachita Baptist. Ulrich was 21.

The Division II school based in Bethany, Oklahoma, did not reveal the cause of death or the nature of Ulrich’s injury. Ulrich was hurt during a 49-14 loss on Saturday, with the game delayed for nearly an hour while he received medical attention before being transported to a hospital.

“It is with heavy hearts that we share the loss of our SNU football player, Tyler Ulrich,” the SNU Athletics said in a post on its X account. “This loss is deeply felt across our campus. Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates, and everyone who knew him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer.”
SNU coach Dustin Hada also posted a tribute on X: “Man of God, ultimate example of quiet strength, loyal, worker, joyous. That’s who Tyler was!!”
The school’s president, Keith Newman, said Ulrich died in the hospital “surrounded by the love, prayers, and presence of his family, teammates and dear friends.”
On Tuesday, SNU held a campuswide prayer chapel in honor of Ulrich.
Ulrich, who was from Azle, Texas, was in his third season at SNU and had 16 starts in 20 games, including six starts this year. He ranked third on the team with 36 tackles.
Southern Nazarene have canceled their game at Southwestern Oklahoma State on Saturday.

body: A year ago, the Brewers were sent home after a 97-win season at the hands of the Dodgers in a clean sweep. Flash forward to Thursday night in Los Angeles, and Milwaukee has gotten its redemption.

The Brewers got back at the Dodgers by sweeping the two-time defending World Series champions from the NLCS, reaching the World Series stage for the first time since 1982. Much was made about the big-name star comparison between the Brewers and Dodgers — but the team without a collection of MVPs and All-Stars advanced.

The Dodgers' star talent, from Shohei Ohtani and Mookie Betts to Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell, have made them the title favorites all year. articles.headline: 34 Years Later, the Best-Ever 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
keyFacts: The author evaluated newspaper comic strips to find the best quote from Gary Larson's The Far Side.
The author determined that Larson's work relied on joke-telling rather than deep, inspirational, or philosophical themes.
The author selected a 1992 cartoon about a mime and a falling tree as the best Far Side quote.
body: In recent months, I’ve been examining the best-ever quotes from various newspaper comic strips, and in that time I’ve determined that every comic strip requires its own approach. For Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, I went with something heartfelt and inspirational because those comics and characters really have inspired people. For Bill Watterson’s Calvin and Hobbes, I investigated something more philosophical, as the best of those comics make the audience contemplate human nature and the world around them. But for Gary Larson’s The Far Side, well, the task is monumentally different.

Larson didn’t do deep. He didn’t do inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful in the lofty sense. They required thought because Larson’s work was brilliant, and you sometimes had to figure out what the punchline was. For example, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly on his glasses. Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

The Far Side was — and remains — brilliant, but it's not the kind of thing that makes you ponder life’s big questions. Larson channeled his genius into joke-telling, and that’s what made The Far Side so sharply funny. As such, determining Larson’s best-ever Far Side quote shouldn’t be some insightful, inspirational, or thoughtful journey — even though I did try going that way at first.

I thought maybe the quote should come from a comic about God, as several Far Side comics feature God as a character. But after reading a whole bunch of Larson’s God comics, I determined that God actually isn’t all that deep or interesting. Sometimes he’s just kind of a jerk.

Then I thought to look up comics about death, thinking that maybe Larson had something profound to say on the subject. Given Larson’s signature macabre style of humor, death is featured frequently in The Far Side, but nothing seemed all that weighty or important. I finally abandoned this approach when I found a comic where a snake hanged himself with his own body.
The Far Side was never meant to be “deep”

That’s when I gave up on going deep and decided to just find something funny. But there are thousands of Far Side comics, and Larson’s humor varied. Sometimes he was dark, sometimes he was silly, sometimes he deconstructed a well-known saying or song or other pop culture reference. So I tried to find a quote that did all — or at least most of — what Larson was known for. Also, I wanted a quote where the visual wasn’t required to get the joke. Larson’s work was highly visual, and with generally just one panel, it often had the visual as the setup and the caption as the punchline. If I was looking for the best ever Far Side comic, it would be one where the visual and the caption work in concert. But while trying to find the best-ever quote, I wanted something where the image was not required.

For a little while I thought about going with “Welcome to hell… here’s your accordion,” from a comic which shows Heaven and Hell. In Heaven, you’re given a harp, but in Hell you’re given an accordion. I liked this because it’s very dark and silly, and it’s the kind of thing you’d only find in The Far Side. Eventually though I softened on it because the visual is still the stronger element in this one. The line comes off as basically a funny non-sequitur without the visual. To get the whole joke about how accordions are terrible instruments, you really need the contrast.
After abandoning that comic, I found this one from 1992 and realized it was the perfect fit. The image shows a mime under a falling tree and the caption reads:
“Question: If a tree falls in the forest and no one’s around, and it hits a mime, does anyone care?”

I think this is the one because it’s funny, because it's dark, because it's silly, and because it takes a well-known idiom — the tree falling in the woods question — and turns it into a punchline. That may not do everything that Larson did, but it’s a lot of his very best qualities all in one place.

And, unlike the vast majority of Far Side comics, it’s more about the words than the image. Larson’s gags were almost always visual, or at least relying on a visual component to get his jokes across. For this comic, I’d argue that you don’t need the visual at all. Sure, the drawing is funny, but in no way is it required. Also, this quote is entirely lacking in emotional or philosophical depth, which is precisely what you want when you’re reading The Far Side.

articles.headline: Three children and teacher killed in US primary school shooting
keyFacts: A 16-year-old boy killed three children and a teacher at an Oregon elementary school before a bystander shot him dead, police said.
Police said a seven-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to a hospital in critical condition.
Bend schools were closed on Friday because officials said the community needed time to heal.
body: - Published
A 16-year-old has shot dead three children and a teacher at a primary school in the US state of Oregon before he was killed by a bystander, police said.
The suspect, who has not been named, forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary School in the city of Bend on Thursday afternoon by shooting at locked doors, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.
The teenager was shot dead by a community member who "pursued him into the school and engaged him", Krantz said.

The three children killed were aged five, eight and 11. A seven-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to a hospital in a critical condition, Krantz said. It is unclear if the attacker had any links to the school.
"We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," Steven Cook, the top administrative official of the local school district, said in a statement.
"No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing."
Police said the attacker was a local 16-year-old boy, but they did not release any further details on him or the identity of the victims.
Police were alerted to an active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary at 12:59 local time (04:59 BST), Bend Police Department spokeswoman Sheila Miller told reporters.
The first call came from a person who said that an unknown suspect was shooting into their car with a long gun, police said. Photos released from the scene show a red truck with bullet holes.
Minutes later, the local county dispatch received 911 calls reporting that the attacker had entered the school.
Police said he shot at locks on the doors in order to force his way inside.
Local media reports suggested the school received new classroom doors in 2022 which can be locked with the flip of a switch.
A bystander saw the shooting begin to unfold, pursued the attacker into the school and shot him dead, police said.
Three minutes later, officers first arrived at the scene. They confirmed that the attacker had been killed, and then searched the school.
Schools in Bend have been closed on Friday. Officials said the community needed time to heal.
Around 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary School, which has more than 40 adult staff members, police said.
According to the K-12 School Shooting Database, there were 235 shooting incidents at American schools last year and at least 140 so far this year.

articles.headline: Maine Senate debate gets testy as Troy Jackson tells Collins to ‘shut up’: Top takeaways
keyFacts: Senator Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson met in Bangor for their fourth and final Maine Senate debate before a live audience.
During an interruption by a protester, Jackson told Collins to "shut up" after she suggested the protester supported him.
Collins defended her voting record, while Jackson acknowledged billionaire campaign support but promised to raise taxes on the wealthy.
body: BANGOR, Maine — The fourth and final debate of the Maine Senate race knocked both candidates off balance as Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) and her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson , met for the first time before a live audience.
The first three debates, held in television studios, were subdued affairs and lacked the fireworks and off-script remarks that defined Thursday night’s event in Bangor.

Jackson at one point told Collins to “shut up” over a protester she said was one of his supporters. Collins, for her part, struggled to name a time when her vote blocked a GOP priority. Both moments were quickly clipped online as fodder for the other side and set the tone for the rest of the debate.
Here are four takeaways from Gracie Theatre, where Collins and Jackson got one last chance to scrutinize each other before the Nov. 3 election.
Jackson tells Collins to ‘shut up’ over protester remark

The most contentious moment of the night came when a protester briefly interrupted the debate to shout at Collins, politely telling her that he was “so sorry to interrupt” but that he is “terrified” about data centers he said were “destroying” the climate.
As the protester was escorted from the room, Collins quipped, “This is obviously one of Troy’s supporters.”
“Oh, shut up,” Jackson replied. “I did not — I don’t even know that kid.”
The protester, a younger man with a badge that said “press,” began to shout more loudly about Collins accepting corporate PAC money as he was removed from the theater.
Collins cites Hegseth when asked for outcome-changing vote
Earlier in the debate, Collins was asked to name a time when she stopped a GOP policy from going through with her vote.

Collins, known for her independent streak in the Senate, said there were a “few examples” before detailing her vote against Pete Hegseth, who was confirmed as war secretary despite her opposition to his nomination.

“At one point, I had organized people to vote against Secretary Hegseth,” Collins said. “As you undoubtedly have read, at the very last minute, one of our Republicans changed his mind. Otherwise, he would’ve been defeated for that job.”
The example was mocked by Democrats as proving Jackson’s argument that Collins only votes against Republicans when it does not affect the outcome.
Collins went on to cite an analysis by the Bangor Daily News finding that her vote proved decisive in 56 instances that benefited Democrats.

“I voted against my own party more often than any other senator on either side of the aisle,” Collins said, before taking a jab at Jackson. “That is not something that Troy could ever say. He’s going to be an automatic vote for the Democrat position, no matter what.”

On the Hegseth vote, Collins appears to be referring to retiring Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC), a Republican who revealed in a new book that he regretted voting to confirm Hegseth at the outset of President Donald Trump’s second term.
Collins was one of three Senate Republicans to vote “no,” alongside Sens. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Mitch McConnell (R-KY), but Democrats needed a fourth for Hegseth’s nomination to be blocked.
Collins stands by RFK Jr. confirmation
At another point, Collins was asked to address her support for Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as health and human services secretary and whether she would vote the same way today.

“I agree with him on some issues, disagree with him on others,” Collins said, telling the moderators that she rejects his vaccine skepticism but supports his focus on chronic disease and healthy eating.
Collins said “no” when pressed if she regretted the confirmation vote, adding that Kennedy was “very helpful” in expediting a lower-income home heating program in Maine.

In the same answer, Collins also discussed her support for Russ Vought’s confirmation as Trump’s budget chief. He and Collins have since butted heads repeatedly, most recently over the administration’s last-minute attempt to cancel funding appropriated by Congress.
“It is true that we fight on a lot of different issues, and I’m pleased to say that I often prevail, such as his proposed cuts on medical research,” Collins said.
Collins is chairwoman of the Senate Appropriations Committee.
Collins and Jackson become the moderators

The moderators covered many of the same topics as prior debates, asking about the war in Iran, immigration enforcement, and the cost of housing. But two of the questions were unique and came directly from the candidates themselves.

Collins, given a chance to ask Jackson a direct question, pressed him on the delay in submitting his financial disclosure reports, suggesting to the audience that he hasn’t been “transparent” and is benefiting from ads paid for by billionaires.
Jackson responded that he would raise taxes on the wealthy, but elicited a gasp when he said Collins was correct about the donor support.
“As far as the billionaires I might have on my campaign, that is accurate,” Jackson said.

“I’m going to tax those billionaires when I get the U.S. Senate, so if they want to give me money during this campaign, I guess that’s up to them,” he added. “But they know that I don’t owe them a thing like Sen. Collins.”
Jackson accused Collins of condescension for his question. He has vented frustration at the times she’s corrected his answers on the debate stage and has tried to portray her as out of touch.
“Is it just me that you look down on or is it working-class people overall?” he said.
DEMOCRATS GIVE BRIAN FITZPATRICK A RUN FOR HIS MONEY IN PENNSYLVANIA HOUSE BATTLEGROUND
“Troy, I don’t look down on you or anyone,” Collins replied, stating that she had worked from the time she was 10 years old.

The audience was quiet for most of the hourlong event, with only a couple of eruptions. Outside Gracie Theatre, the site of the debate in Bangor, supporters of both Collins and Jackson gathered beforehand with signs and banners. One anti-Collins banner said “Let Them Eat Road Salt,” a reference to Jackson’s viral comment on tariffs.

articles.headline: China tells Israel to stop ‘forced establishment’ of West Bank settlements
keyFacts: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel must stop and reverse West Bank settlements.

Wang and Herzog discussed the war on Iran, with talks covering the need for diplomatic solutions and political settlements.
body: China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi has told Israeli President Isaac Herzog during a meeting in Azerbaijan that Israel should stop and reverse its “forced establishment” of West Bank settlements, China’s foreign ministry said in a statement.
Wang told Herzog that China has consistently viewed the Palestinian question as the greatest historical injustice of this century, the ministry said in the statement on Friday.

Wang emphasised that the “two-state solution” is the right path to a resolution and said the immediate priority is to fully open access to the Gaza Strip so a humanitarian “catastrophe” is not allowed to spread.
Wang added that China is willing to work with the international community to push all parties to return to dialogue as soon as possible and seek a political settlement.

Wang is attending the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia, held in Baku, Azerbaijan, as the special representative of President Xi Jinping, China’s state news agency Xinhua reported.
China urges new Middle East framework

In September, Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Cairo for the first time in a decade and called on Middle East countries to oppose external influence and consider reshaping the region’s security order.
Xi’s rare visit arrived as Beijing seeks to expand its influence in the region amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

The talks covered the US-Israel war on Iran, with both presidents urging “diplomatic solutions” to reach a “comprehensive agreement to end the war”, according to a statement from Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s spokesperson.

In March, China criticised the US and Israeli attacks on Iran, with Beijing demanding an immediate halt to the joint attacks. Wang told his Israeli counterpart, Gideon Saar, that the attack on Iran came as negotiations between Washington and Tehran had “made significant progress, including addressing Israel’s security concerns”, China’s foreign ministry said in a statement following the start of the war.

China was Iran’s largest trading partner, buying up to 90 percent of its oil, according to the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission. In 2021, Beijing signed a 25-year “comprehensive strategic partnership agreement” with Tehran.

At the same time, Beijing has spent the past decade cultivating closer ties with Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, and remains a top trade partner of both the US and Israel.

articles.headline: Trump says he’s ‘not a big fan’ of Zelensky after new strikes on Russian oil refineries

body: President Donald Trump expressed his personal distaste for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday after Ukraine launched new strikes on Russian oil refineries.
“I’m not a big fan of Zelensky,” Trump told Newsmax host Rob Finnerty in an exclusive interview. “They’ve destroyed that country.”

Trump announced an energy ceasefire earlier this week, trying to prevent further attacks on Russian and Ukrainian energy infrastructure. The supposed ceasefire wasn’t effective, however, because Russia never agreed to it. Ukraine initially held up its end of the deal before Zelensky ordered the resumption of strikes against Russia.
Moscow carried out strikes on Kyiv for days after Trump announced the energy ceasefire on Sunday. Now the truce is no more.
“Zelensky is not a good guy for us to deal with,” Trump said, blaming former President Joe Biden for giving Zelensky billions of dollars in aid.

. @POTUS : "Zelensky is not a good guy for us to deal with… If they're going to end up with a settlement of some kind, they're not going to do it with him. He doesn't want to settle. He says he wants to settle, but he doesn't." pic.twitter.com/jVbg0jRJg0
— Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) October 16, 2026

Trump also blamed former President Barack Obama for forcing Ukraine to let Russia annex the Crimean Peninsula in 2014. Trump frequently points to the annexation as the moment that Russian President Vladimir Putin didn’t respect the United States because there wasn’t going to be a strong American response to Moscow’s seizure of the strategic peninsula at the time.

Trump has been trying to end the Russia-Ukraine war since he returned to the White House last year, but the task has proven to be particularly challenging due to the deep-seated hatred between Putin and Zelensky.

“When you have that kind of hatred, it’s very hard to get something settled,” Trump said. But if there is going to be a settlement, Trump believes Zelensky shouldn’t be involved because he “doesn’t want to settle.”
Trump hopes the conflict will end soon, saying both leaders want the same result. However, the president noted how he finds it “more difficult to deal with” Zelensky than Putin.

Trump has been more charitable to Putin recently, drawing sharp bipartisan criticism as he distances himself from Zelensky. Last weekend, Trump called on Zelensky to step down and let Ukraine hold an election for a new president. Zelensky said he will organize a presidential election if Russia agrees to a two-month ceasefire. Moscow remains opposed to the idea.

Trump and Zelensky have also been at odds over reports of the U.S. allegedly cutting off Ukraine’s access to intelligence and Starshield, SpaceXAI’s military-grade Starlink satellite network. The defense restrictions hampered Ukraine’s ability to protect itself from Russian strikes.

SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk said that while the aerospace company developed the Starshield system, it is owned by the Department of War . Therefore, any Starshield restrictions imposed on Ukraine would be up to the Trump administration.
The order to limit the satellite network came from inside the White House, Reuters reported on Thursday based on two U.S. officials and a Western official. It is unclear whether Trump gave the order.

Elsewhere in the Newsmax interview, Trump echoed the comments of a Ukrainian woman who slammed Zelensky for letting the war persist.

“President Zelensky has destroyed our country,” he said, recalling the woman’s words. “President Zelensky has taken our men away from us. Our men have no legs, no arms. Our men are, in many cases, in mental institutions or they’re dead.”

body: Ilhan Omar’s husband snaps over allegations she fled US after DC home was raided by feds
By
Hannah Brennan, Fox News
Published Oct. 15, 2026, 10:12 p.m. ET
See more of our coverage in your search results.

While Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., has not been seen publicly since federal agents raided her Washington, D.C., residence on Monday, her political consultant husband was once again spotted emerging from their shared rental home this week.

Tim Mynett was seen Wednesday stepping out in the neighborhood to walk their Golden Labrador Retriever dog Teddy, a second time later that same day to take out the trash and a third time to walk out his wife’s staffer.
“There are rumors that the congresswoman left the country, is that true?” Mynett was asked while on an evening walk with Teddy.

“You guys are annoying the hell out of all the neighbors around here, man,” he told Fox News Digital when approached about the developments this week, including President Donald Trump weighing in on the saga.

One of Omar’s congressional staffers was captured the same day bringing into the couple’s home two large bags from fast food chain Burger King. Security escorted her to the door and staked out in front of the house after she entered with the meal.

Rumors swirled that Omar fled from the country following the raid carried out by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) as part of a criminal fraud investigation looking into the Somali-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork, as first reported by Fox News Digital.
Omar’s cellphone and passport were reportedly seized by federal authorities during the search.

The congresswoman’s staff helped to get her birth year adjusted from 1981 to 1982 in the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library, according to reporters. Omar gained citizenship automatically through her father’s naturalization since she was reportedly 17 years old at the time. If Omar was born in 1981, she would have been 18 years old, meaning the validity of her citizenship could be threatened because she was no longer a minor.
The altered birthdate was published during her entire time serving in Minnesota’s House and for months into her time serving in Congress.

When asked about the federal investigation earlier this week, Mynett told Fox News Digital he has “no concerns” about what federal authorities will find on his wife while investigating her immigration pathway.
“My wife came here when she was 12 years old as a child war refugee,” Mynett said. “No concerns.”

His comments to Fox News Digital come after Omar’s relatives were reportedly issued subpoenas as part of HSI’s investigation into the congresswoman’s immigration paperwork. At least two of Omar’s relatives were subpoenaed, one of which is reportedly Omar’s sister, Sahra Noor.

Fox News Digital asked Mynett about President Donald Trump publicly questioning Omar’s net worth by alleging on Truth Social that her accountant may have reported fraudulent money when her previous financial disclosure listed the couple’s shared net worth as high as $30 million.

“Why did Ilhan Omar report a Net Worth of up to 30 Million Dollars just a short time ago, and then immediately say, “Oh, I made a mistake! It’s really $100,000.” Could it be that her highly paid accountant actually reported the money that was stolen from her fraudulent activities in Minnesota? Would something like that be possible? Do you think the accountant actually gave the right number the first time, 30 Million Dollars, and then she was forced to disavow because she never would have been able to report where that much money came from? She must have freaked out when she saw that money!” Trump posted to Truth Social on Tuesday.

“Where did her house come from, where did her cars come from, and what about her lovely place in Washington, D.C.? I didn’t know that Congressmen and women made that kind of money, but I do know her husband, according to information and belief, makes almost nothing, so it couldn’t have come from him. How many people did she illegally bring into our Country from Somalia? America wants answers, and we want them, NOW!”
Mynett is at the center of yet another investigation into Omar — this time looking into her finances.
Following Monday’s HSI raid, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro said Tuesday that her office is also investigating Omar’s financial disclosures about reporting of her and Mynett’s shared net worth.

Scrutiny of Omar’s finances intensified after her 2024 congressional financial disclosure listed business interests associated with Mynett valued between $6 million and $30 million. Omar’s office subsequently said the figures were incorrect and amended the filing.

The largest change in the documents was from Mynett’s assets. His reported ownership interests in both his winery and venture capital advisory firm, which were previously valued in the millions of dollars, are listed with no value now.

Omar’s office previously told Fox News Digital that Mynett has partners in both businesses and said the earlier disclosure mistakenly reflected the businesses’ total equity rather than his ownership interest. The office also said the original filing listed assets without accounting for liabilities.

articles.headline: The Tesla Roadster flew, drove upside down, and hit 60mph in under a second
keyFacts: Tesla demonstrated its next-generation Roadster in Waco, Texas, where the electric supercar drove upside down, flew briefly, and accelerated to 60mph in under a second.
CEO Elon Musk stated that the Roadster could go into production in 2028, though the company admitted the flying version will not be road legal.
Tesla updated its website with three performance tiers for the Roadster, ranging from a road-ready variant to an invite-only rocket model equipped with cold-gas thrusters.
body: Elon Musk promised a flying car. And the Tesla Roadster did exactly that.
The Tesla Roadster flew, drove upside down, and hit 60mph in under a second
The next-gen Roadster has been in development for nearly a decade. But perhaps it was worth the wait.

Tesla demonstrated its next-generation Roadster at an event in Waco, Texas, where the electric supercar drove upside down, briefly flew, and accelerated to 60mph in under a second. It was an impressive demonstration of a car that likely will come with some heavy caveats and restrictions if it ever goes into production.

The event was less than 30 minutes and felt more like a stunt show than a product reveal. Indeed, there was no mention of price, release date, or other such mundane details. Musk promised the hypercar would go into production in 2028, but after nearly nine years who’s counting. The people were here to see a car fly, and that’s what Tesla gave them.

First, the Roadster drove up a very tall, multi-story ramp, using its incredible downforce to cling to the vertical roadway. When it reached the top of the ramp, it flipped around using its cold-gas thrusters to bring it gently back down to earth. The car uses a fan-based suction system, supplied by SpaceX and mounted underneath the vehicle, which is capable of generating up to two Gs of suction force.

Next, the Roadster flew over the rest of Tesla’s lineup, including the Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck, Semi, and Cybercab — doing what Tesla VP for Engineering Lars Moravy called “a kick flip” in the process. Musk explained that it features attitude-control thrusters as well as main thrusters at the rear, giving the Roadster rocket-like capabilities.

“So it can basically fly like a rocket,” Musk said. “And it could do rolls. It could do, like, crazy gymnastics. Whatever you want, really. Now, I should say that this is not necessarily a safety-optimized car. But it takes the fun meter to 11 out of 10.”

The Roadster two ultra-high pressure air tanks with a combined volume of 600 liters, containing approximately 250 kilograms of air, and uses 10 nozzles to execute its maneuvers. The Roadster can even recharge its own tank, without requiring a specialized chemical propellant. The stored compressed air supplies the thrust needed to lift the car and perform the demonstrated maneuvers.

Musk claimed “This will be an actual car that’s on the roads” — though later the company admitted it would not be road legal. This seems obvious, of course. Imagine having to satisfy strict regulatory requirements from the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The Roadster could go into production in 2028, as Musk promised — or it could be another decade of missed deadlines and broken promises. Again, who cares? Car flew.

As for the Roadster itself, Musk called it “the last best driver’s car.” Moravy said that Tesla drew inspiration from aerospace designs such as the SR-71 reconnaissance aircraft. It’s a two-seater, with seats molded directly into the chassis. Its steering and driving controls use steer-by-wire technology, including a steer-by-wire yoke, brakes, and throttle. The rear of the car features the thrusters and fans housed around the diffuser area. And it has a retractable rear wing for added downforce.

Tesla has also said that the Roadster can accelerate from 0-60mph in less than a second. And during the event, the company claimed it did so in 0.81 seconds. Musk explained that increasing the applied force while reducing the vehicle’s mass help boost acceleration. In fact, Musk says the production Roadster should improve on the demonstrated result, although he acknowledged the extreme forces involved and the need to avoid subjecting occupants to extreme acceleration.
“You’ve got to crack halfway to the speed of sound, I think,” Musk teased. “Mach 0.5. Maybe a little higher.”

After the event, Tesla updated its website with details about the three distinct performance tiers for the next-generation Roadster, outlining how its controversial cold-gas thruster systems scale across the lineup:

- Performance (Road Ready): The entry-level variant seats two passengers and relies on an active aerodynamics package paired with a multi-mode suction system to maximize downforce on and off the track. It claims a 0–60 mph time under 1.6 seconds and a target range exceeding 300 miles.

- Thrust (Race Ready): Also a two-seater, this mid-tier version pairs the multi-mode suction system with rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters. The additional propulsion cuts the vehicle’s 0–60 mph acceleration to under 0.9 seconds. Tesla says this configuration will be in “limited release.”

- Rocket (Air Ready): The single-seat flagship model expands the hardware to a full perimeter-mounted array of cold-gas thrusters. In addition to driving forward and upward acceleration, the thrusters enable lateral and rotational movement in midair — enabling the short, low-altitude stunts showcased at the event. This top-spec version reaches a top speed over 230 mph and pushes 0–60 mph acceleration to under 0.59 seconds. Tesla says this version will be “invite only,” but also “not approved for public road use.”

The next-gen Roadster certainly took the scenic route in getting here. A prototype version was announced as a “one more thing” style surprise during the 2017 Tesla Semi event. The specs sounded ludicrous even back then: 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds, a top speed over 250 mph, a 200 kWh battery delivering up to 620 miles of range, and a $200,000 starting price tag. Musk said deliveries would start in 2020, which sounded perfectly doable at the time.

Early adopters quickly threw down $50,000 deposits (or $250,000 for the limited Founders Series), effectively interest-free loans to help fund Tesla’s scaling ambitions. But then Tesla seemed to forget about the Roadster, as cementing its status as the ultimate vaporware. Production deadlines slipped as Tesla prioritized mass-market vehicles like the Model Y, while also wrestling with the overly complicated Cybertruck. Occasionally, when Musk would remember that the Roadster existed, he would up the ante about its capabilities. This culminated in the “SpaceX package” that would equip the supercar with cold-gas thrusters, bestowing hover powers and a 0-60 time under one second.

Musk has also sought to downplay the Roadster’s significance, calling it a “small potato situation” that will not “move the needle in a major way financially.” He’s framed the supercar more as a joint engineering collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, even questioning whether it’s “even a car anymore” given its experimental nature. Some analysts theorize that the decision to re-release the Roadster is an attempt to set the stage for a rumored Tesla-SpaceX merger.

Tesla’s failure to bring the Roadster to market allowed other automakers to slip past the company with their own hyper-powered EVs. Rimac has smashed performance records with the Nevera, Porsche has refined electric performance with the Taycan, and Chinese giants like BYD are producing track-ready supercars at a fraction of the cost. The Roadster is no longer shocking the world as an impossible prototype; it’s playing catch-up to an industry that spent nine years building what Tesla merely rendered.
But then again, none of those cars flew.

articles.headline: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
keyFacts: Tesla revealed a redesigned second-generation Roadster featuring SpaceX thrusters that CEO Elon Musk demonstrated can lift and spin the vehicle.
Musk stated that Tesla will build the long-delayed vehicle in 2028, offering it in three trims with prices ranging from $50,000 for reservations.
Engineering VP Lars Moravy said the Roadster uses 10 thrusters connected to compressed air tanks to enable midair maneuvers.
body: Tesla just revealed its redesigned second-generation Roadster with SpaceX thrusters, a vehicle CEO Elon Musk has called “the best of the last of the human-driven cars.”

Musk showed off the car at an event outside Waco, Texas, with a demonstration that saw the car use a mixture of high-powered fans and thrusters to drive up an inverted ramp, spin around, and ease itself to a landing on the pavement below. The car also used the thrusters to lift itself over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 while in motion.

“This will be the actual car that’s on the roads,” Musk said of the car, which Tesla showed accelerating 0 to 60 miles per hour in one second. “It literally is just going to puff itself up, and uh, and be able to do this, these maneuvers whenever you’d like.”

Musk said Tesla will finally build the long-delayed vehicle in 2028, but didn’t name a price. Tesla will offer it in three trims. The first is “Performance,” which Tesla describes as “road ready.” It seats two, has active aerodynamics, and features a “multi-mode suction system for next-level performance on and off the track.” The second trim is “Thrust,” which is “race ready” and seats two, and has rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters that enable sub-one-second 0-to-60 mph accleration. The third is “Rocket,” which is “air ready” and seats one, and has 10 cold-gas thrusters positioned around the car.
All three trims will have 300 miles of range and be capable of speeds exceeding 230 miles per hour.
Tesla’s website showed Thursday the company is taking reservations for the car, charging $50,000 just to reserve the Performance, and $250,000 for Thrust. The Rocket trim is billed as “invite only.”

Engineering VP Lars Moravy said at the event that the Roadster uses 10 thrusters connected to 600 liters of compressed air to lift and spin the car in midair. The air tank can be recharged, he said. “Every usable void in the car is packed with Carbon Fiber Overwrapped Pressure Vessels (COPVs),” Tesla wrote in a post on X, referring to the type of pressure vessel that has been at the root of multiple SpaceX rocket explosions. The company said “every usable void” in the car is filled with these vessels.
Musk also said at the event that Tesla may try to jump the Snake River Canyon — the site of Evel Knievel’s famous attempt to cross the gorge in a steam-powered rocket.

Musk has positioned the Roadster as a true halo car for Tesla, saying at one point that he’s “not sure it moves the needle massively from a revenue standpoint.” But he has previously said that “safety is not the main goal” with the new Roadster.

“If you buy a Ferrari, safety is not the number one goal. I say, if safety is your number one goal, do not buy the Roadster,” he said on a podcast earlier this year. Tesla would “aspire not to kill anyone in this car,” he said.

“This is the culmination of incredible work by Tesla and SpaceX Engineers working closely together to make something you haven’t seen in any movie, better than any James Bond car,” Musk said at the event. “I’ve never seen anything like this. You know when I suggested this to the team, I thought, ‘Am I crazy?’”
Musk had previously claimed that the car “will be very different from what was shown previously” and promised the demo would be the “most exciting, whether it works or not, demo ever of any product.”

The design changes were notable. The car, shown in stark white, now has a more angular design reminiscent of a Lamborghini or the famous Lotus Esprit used by the James Bond character in The Spy Who Loved Me — a car Musk owns, which was on display at the event.
In another post, Tesla said the design was inspired by the SR-71 reconnaissance aircraft and the F-35 fighter jet.
“Our design language has evolved since the last reveal: from S3XY to Cybertruck, Cybercab & Optimus,” the company wrote.

Tesla held the event almost nine years to the day after the company first revealed the second-generation Roadster, a modernized take on its first-ever car. Unveiled as a surprise at the end of the Tesla Semi reveal in 2017, the revamped Roadster was supposed to be delivered in just a few years. Tesla allowed customers to place $50,000 deposits to reserve the car. Some even paid $250,000 to reserve one of 1,000 “Founders Series” versions.

Musk first talked about adding thrusters to the car in 2018. “SpaceX option package for new Tesla Roadster will include ~10 small rocket thrusters arranged seamlessly around car,” he wrote on Twitter that year. “These rocket engines dramatically improve acceleration, top speed, braking & cornering. Maybe they will even allow a Tesla to fly …”

But the Roadster project took a back seat. In 2018, Tesla suffered through what Musk eventually dubbed “production hell” with the Model 3 sedan. The company then moved onto other projects like the Model Y SUV, which became the best-selling vehicle in the world, and the Cybertruck, which was a commercial flop by Tesla’s own standards. Along the way, Musk delayed the new Roadster in 2020, 2021, 2023, and 2024.

As more time passed following the launch of those new vehicles, Musk started talking about the second-generation Roadster again. Late last year, he said on Joe Rogan’s podcast that he wanted to reveal it by the end of 2025. One week later, at the shareholder meeting where he was awarded a $1 trillion pay package, he delayed it to April 1, 2026. Musk said holding an April Fools’ Day event would give him “some deniability” if Tesla delayed the event again.
“Like, I could say I was just kidding,” he said at the time. Tesla wound up pushing back the reveal again. It attempted to hold the event on October 1, but severe weather forced yet another delay.
These repeated delays caused a number of high-profile customers to speak out over the years, including YouTuber Marques Brownlee and OpenAI head Sam Altman.

“They really just got on stage and said this newly designed 4000+ pound car can do flips and go half the speed of sound (380+mph) and will ship in 2028,” Brownlee posted Thursday. “This is a prank, right?”

articles.headline: 'Oh, shut up!': Democrat snaps at Collins after heckler drives Maine Senate debate off the rails
keyFacts: A protester interrupted the final Maine Senate debate between Republican Senator Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson to shout about climate concerns.
Collins suggested the demonstrator was a supporter of Jackson, prompting Jackson to snap back at her during the heated exchange.
The close Senate race is considered a toss-up and a top flip opportunity for Democrats in the midterm elections.
body: A protester interrupted the final debate between Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson in Maine, triggering a heated exchange after Collins suggested the demonstrator was a Jackson supporter.

The interruption came amid a debate that saw the candidates trade fire over numerous issues. The race between Jackson and Collins, who is seeking a sixth term representing the blue-leaning Northern New England state, is a top flip opportunity for Democrats as they try to win back the Senate majority from Republicans in the midterm elections.

The latest public opinion polls indicate a race within the margin of error between Collins and Jackson, a one-time logger and former state Senate president. The latest Fox News Power Rankings rate the race as a toss-up, as do leading nonpartisan political handicappers the Cook Political Report, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball.
DEMS SEE NEW CHANCES TO FLIP SENATE SEATS BUT GOP'S MASSIVE CASH ADVANTAGE AN OBSTACLE
The protester, who interrupted Collins as she spoke, yelled out, "I'm terrified. AI data centers are destroying our climate. They are poisoning our water."
"30 years for what?" the demonstrator shouted, referring to Collins’ tenure in the Senate.
As security escorted the protester out of the debate hall, Collins suggested the man was a Jackson supporter.
"So, this is obviously one of Troy's supporters," Collins said.
Jackson quickly fired back, "Oh, shut up, I did not — I didn't, I don't even know who that kid."
Another heated moment came a few minutes later when each candidate was able to ask a question of the other.
Jackson, who grew up in rural northern Maine in the same county as Collins, asked, "What I'm curious about — is it just me that you look down on, or is it working-class people overall?"
DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING - HERE ARE THREE FACTORS THAT COULD STOP IT
The senator shot back, "Troy, I do not look down on you or on anyone. I grew up in Caribou. My first job was picking potatoes."

As he works to oust Collins from the Senate, Jackson has repeatedly tried to anchor the senator to President Donald Trump , who has seen his approval ratings in Maine and across the country drop further underwater.
"The reality is 100% of the time when Donald Trump needs her, Susan Collins is going to be there," Jackson claimed.
But Collins pointed to what she described as a "major difference between Troy and me. I vote very independently. ... I am the most bipartisan member of the Senate."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
And referring to Jackson, Collins said, "We don’t need more people who are going to vote a straight party line."

Collins and Jackson spent much of the hour-long debate trading fire on issues, including the Iran War, immigration, rising fuel prices and electricity rates, budget deficits, Supreme Court reform, dark money in politics, an assault weapons ban and climate change.

Collins used the debate, the fourth between the two candidates over a two-week period, but the first with a live audience, to once again showcase how her Senate seniority has helped her deliver federal funding for Maine. Meanwhile, Jackson used the showdown to position himself as an outsider who understands the struggles and frustrations of working-class voters.

Jackson won a special nominating convention in late July to claim the party's Senate nomination, which was left vacant after primary winner Graham Platner ended his campaign following allegations he raped a woman he previously dated. Platner denied the allegations but dropped out.
Jackson, who earlier this year unsuccessfully ran for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination, had campaigned alongside Platner during the primary campaign.
Collins, who is the only GOP senator seeking re-election in a state Trump lost in the 2024 election, has a history of surviving Democratic efforts to unseat her.

Six years ago, she trailed Democratic challenger Sara Gideon, the Maine House speaker at the time, but Collins won re-election by nearly nine points while former President Joe Biden carried the state by a similar margin.

articles.headline: US lawmaker calls videogame purchases rentals disguised as sales: 'When you pay for a game, you should own it'
keyFacts: US Representative Ritchie Torres announced plans to introduce the Power To The Players Act.
Torres' office stated the bill directs the Federal Trade Commission to regulate consumer ownership, playing rights, and game transfers.
The proposed legislation aims to secure genuine game ownership and require offline modes before online games are shut down.
body: US Representative Ritchie Torres, a Democrat from New York City, announced today that he will introduce the "Power To The Players Act."
If it becomes law, the bill will see the US Federal Trade Commission create regulations that protect our "ability to own and play" purchased games, according to Torres' office.

"When you pay for a game, you should own it," says Torres. "Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale."

The game ownership issue is longstanding on PC, which moved to digital distribution a couple decades ago, but has recently come to the foreground of public consciousness as the consoles also transition away from discs. Earlier this year, Sony announced that it will end physical disc production in 2028.

The related problem of online games being decommissioned before players are done with them has also received more attention in recent years. The Stop Killing Games campaign in particular has raised the issue's profile, arguing that basic offline functionality should be expected when online games are retired. Founder Ross Scott and organizer Moritz Katzner gained an audience with the European Parliament earlier this year.

As one of its prime examples of the problem, Stop Killing Games has pointed to The Crew, a Ubisoft racing game which went offline in 2024, preventing those who purchased it from continuing to play even the singleplayer campaign.

The aim of the Power To The Players Act is to establish and enforce a more genuine ownership of purchased games, as opposed to the revocable licenses we currently buy, and to require that offline modes be made available before online games are shut down.
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

For DRM-free games, such as those purchased from GOG, ownership is a non-issue: Once you have the game files, you can back them up and use them for as long as you can find a PC that'll run them. Realistically, the FTC is not going to mandate the eradication of software copy protection, so if passed the bill would presumably arrive at a softer definition of ownership.
I've reached out to Rep Torres' office for more information on what enforcement of the bill is expected to look like, should it pass.

Tyler grew up in Silicon Valley during the '80s and '90s, playing games like Zork and Arkanoid on early PCs. He was later captivated by Myst, SimCity, Civilization, Command & Conquer, all the shooters they call "boomer shooters" now, and PS1 classic Bushido Blade (that's right: he had Bleem!). Tyler joined PC Gamer in 2011, and today he's focused on the site's news coverage. His hobbies include amateur boxing and adding to his 1,200-plus hours in Rocket League.

articles.headline: Did AI Just Erase an Entire Swedish TV Show?
keyFacts: TV4 announced that the return of The Challenge: Sweden has been delayed indefinitely after edited episodes were lost.
Program director Mia Lindqvist stated that production company Mastiff experienced a backup system failure, though network officials disputed reports that an AI agent acted independently.
Production teams must now recut the series from scratch using the remaining raw materials.
body: Fans of TV4’s international edition of The Challenge, which features Swedish celebrities competing in physical and mental contests, will have to wait for another season. An AI agent reportedly deleted edited episodes of the show, and a TV4 backup system failure wiped out hundreds of hours of work.
The Swedish series was due to return on Nov. 22, but has been delayed indefinitely, TV4 said in a statement.
“We have to recut it from scratch. All the raw material is still there, and all that,” program director Mia Lindqvist said on the network’s website.
More from CNET

According to translated articles, the network denies an Aftonbladet report that an AI agent deleted the episodes. However, while TV4’s Lindqvist told the newspaper that an AI agent didn’t act independently, she did not deny that AI was involved in the mishap. Still, she blamed the failed backup system.
“The big problem is that (production company) Mastiff’s backup didn’t work,” she said.
A representative for TV4 didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The program features stars of other Swedish reality programs, such as the country’s version of The Bachelor and Farmen, a reality show about (wait for it…) contestants on a farm. The Challenge: Sweden first aired in 2023.

AI is increasingly a part of editing and production workflows across movies and television, with entertainment giants, including Netflix, leaning on the technology to produce content more quickly and at lower cost.

If an AI agent were somehow responsible, that would seem to have negated any of AI’s time-saving benefits for The Challenge: Sweden and its production team, who now have to spend time rebuilding the episode edits that were lost.

articles.headline: 'I Just Sort of Disconnect' — Jeff Kaplan is Avoiding Overwatch at all Costs
keyFacts: Former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan said he completely avoids online discussions, subreddits, and videos about the game to protect his mental health.
Kaplan stated in an interview with GameSpot that he has not played Overwatch since April 2021 after leaving Blizzard.
Kaplan is currently working on an open world action-survival shooter called The Legend of California at his own studio.
body: Former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan explained how he protects his psyche by completely avoiding online discussions and subreddits about Blizzard's hero shooter.

If you’re a die-hard Overwatch player, you’re likely familiar with the name Jeff Kaplan. He was essentially the face of the game for years, endearing fans with his regular developer updates and memorable interactions with its fanbase.

After leaving Blizzard in 2021 , Kaplan founded his own game development studio and is currently working on an open world, action-survival shooter called The Legend of California. He has firmly put Overwatch behind him — to the point where he avoids interacting with it at all costs online.
“With Overwatch, I had a very almost clinical separation, knowing how the WoW thing had gone,” Kaplan said in a recent interview with GameSpot . “I’ve literally not played the game since April 2021.

“I don’t, for my own psyche, I don’t read the subreddits. After I said my goodbye to competitive Overwatch and the Overwatch subreddit, I never go back and read. I don’t watch YouTube [videos]. I don’t search for my name in Overwatch. I don’t search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect. I actually tell all the algorithms like, ‘Yeah, I’m not really interested in Overwatch anymore. I know you think I’m the Overwatch guy, but like, that’s just not for me anymore.'”

He told the outlet that it was surprisingly more painful for him to leave the World of Warcraft team to work on Overwatch than it was to put the hero shooter in his rear view, calling it a “training moment” for taking the next step in his career.

“WoW was who I was at that point,” he explained. “I worked every minute, every waking minute, on WoW. If I wasn’t working on WoW, I was playing WoW. And every time I played WoW, I had this notepad next to the desk that I’d be filling out to walk in the next morning and go, ‘These are all the things we need to change.’ It was kind of shocking in a very negative emotional way to step away from WoW, because it was such a part of who I was and how I identified. It was who I was as a game developer.”
After learning the hard way that the games he worked on didn’t belong to him, but were instead an IP under Blizzard’s ownership, it was easier for him to move forward.

“Overwatch happened. I was a part of it. There’s a group there now, and Overwatch is now about them. Both the players and the developers, that’s their Overwatch now. They’re making it, they own it, they play it. I’m onto this new thing, and that’s where I’m at in my life,” he said.

Kaplan hasn’t shied away from sharing his thoughts on the current gaming industry since making his exit from Blizzard almost half a decade ago. Most recently, he had some harsh words for players who complain about games they’ll never actually play.
"If a game comes out, and you don't want to play it, and you've never played it? Shut the f*** up. No one cares,” he said.
And in March, he revealed the reason why he actually left Blizzard behind, describing a specific meeting that he called “the biggest f*** you moment I had in my career.”

articles.headline: Porn showing choking or incest to be banned from early November, government says
keyFacts: The UK government announced that online pornography depicting strangulation, incest, or adult role-play as children will become illegal starting November 6.
Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones stated that the ban aims to prevent online porn from normalising violence against women and shaping unhealthy relationship views.
Violating the new rules carries maximum prison sentences of up to five years for publication and up to three years for possession.
body: - Published
Online pornography depicting strangulation or incestuous relationships will be banned from early November, the government has announced.

From 6 November, it will be illegal to possess or publish porn which shows strangulation or suffocation, depicts sexual activity between people who are related or shows adults role-playing as children under 16.
The new rules follow a review into porn regulation in 2025 which found depictions of choking were "rife" on popular porn sites and had helped normalise the act among young people.
Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin, who headed the review, said the news came "not a moment too soon".

She told the Press Association the change in law would "send the unequivocal signal" to companies that host and facilitate porn, and also to wider society, that "extreme and violent content that encourages real-life harm is not acceptable".
Her independent review, commissioned by former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak's government, cited an account of a 14-year-old boy asking a teacher how to choke girls during sex.
It warned that people imitating such behaviour "may face devastating consequences".
Non-fatal strangulation is already an offence if someone does not consent - but its depiction online is currently not illegal.
Amendments to the Crime and Policing Bill, which became law in April, sought to ensure such content would be captured by the legislation and made criminal offences in England and Wales.
Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones said it was not about "criminalising harmless sexual preferences".

But she said "porn can shape what people think a healthy relationship looks like, especially young people". Content which "normalises, or even glorifies" violence against women can "blur the line with what is acceptable in real life", she said.
"If you've got this material, delete it. If you're sharing it, stop," Davies-Jones added.
"It's not as harmless as you may think, and after 6 November, it is criminal."
The new offences each carry a maximum penalty of five years' imprisonment, for publication.
According to the government, this could include uploading, posting or otherwise making the content available to someone online.
Possession, meanwhile, could include keeping an image stored on a phone, computer or in cloud storage, the government says.
Someone found to be in possession of images depicting sexual activity involving a person pretending to be under 16 could face up to three years' imprisonment, after 6 November.
Those found to be in possession of images depicting strangulation, suffocation or penetrative sexual activity between certain relatives could face up to two years' imprisonment.
Porn that shows or depicts sex between step or foster-relations where one person is pretending to be under 18 will also be captured by the new offences.
Durham University law professor Clare McGlynn - who has previously warned widely available extreme content normalises sexual violence - welcomed the laws taking full effect.

"This is a potential turning point, the commencement of these laws marking a line in the sand when we decided that we were no longer going to accept the normalisation of sexually violent content in pornography," she told the BBC.
But she said questions remained over how swiftly tech platforms and regulators would act to remove and mitigate the spread of violating material.

"While these are criminal offences, this is not about prosecuting individuals, but transforming the online pornographic landscape and that requires the platforms and regulator to act," Prof McGlynn added.
Additional reporting by Chris Vallance

articles.headline: O'Neill defiant in defeat but Celtic's 'flat-track bullies' fail another big test
keyFacts: Celtic lost 4-1 to Benfica in the Europa League after conceding three goals in the first half due to defensive errors.
Manager Martin O'Neill stated he remains determined and believes his team can still reach the knockout stages despite the slow start.
Celtic currently sit 34th out of 36 teams in the competition after losing all four of their high-stakes matches this season.
body: - Published

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill chose to focus on the second-half positives from his side's 4-1 Europa League defeat by Benfica and insisted they can still reach the knockout stages despite their slow start.
In stark contrast, Chris Sutton branded his former side as "flat-track bullies".
Celtic have lost four of their past five games. Every high-stakes match this term - both meetings with Rangers and both European outings - has ended in a defeat.
By the time their performance improved in Lisbon on Thursday, they were three goals down and effectively already out of the contest, hamstrung by their own sloppy mistakes.
Dane Murray upended Jhon Duran to concede a penalty inside four minutes, an error which characterised the first 45 minutes.
Sebastian Tounekti then allowed Alexander Bah to run past him for Benfica's second and goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo was beaten too easily as Duran scored the hosts' third.
Camilo Duran pulled one back after the break and struck a post as the Scottish champions improved, but Vangelis Pavlidis struck Benfica's fourth late on to kill any faint Celtic hopes.
"Last thing you want to do is concede so early on," O'Neill said. "We could've capitulated, but I thought the second-half performance was terrific. We created chance after chance.
"The second-half performance gives me the determination... I think we can still qualify. We can still do it.
"We came roaring back. We could've scored a number of goals. I accept on the break they could have scored themselves, as they did with their fourth goal."
Even the most ardent Celtic supporters would struggle to share their manager's optimism given they sit 34th of 36 teams in the competition after two games.
Captain Callum McGregor admitted Celtic were masters of their own downfall in the first half.
"First half we didn't help ourselves," he told TNT Sports. "Unforced errors lead to the second and third goals and you have a mountain to climb.
"We know at this level if you don't look after the ball you're going to get punished."
'I'd pick Duran over Hogh every day of the week'
Although Celtic conceded four, the scoreline did not flatter Benfica. The Portuguese side created chances aplenty in both halves and hit the woodwork twice in addition to their four goals.
Celtic's lack of depth in defence was exposed once again in the absence of the injured Cameron Carter-Vickers as Gianluca Prestianni and Duran tormented the visitors' back four.
However, it is in forward areas where O'Neill perhaps has his biggest headache.
Club record signing Kasper Hogh was hooked at half-time and has now failed to score in 10 of his first 11 outings since joining from Bodo/Glimt in the summer.
Duran shifted inside for the second half and posed far more of a threat than his Danish team-mate.
"If I'm a creative midfield player and I've got Duran and Hogh to pick from, I'm taking Duran every day of the week," former Celtic midfielder Scott Allan said.
"He looks to get off the side of defenders, if you put a ball in the area, he's more likely to be alive to it.
"Hogh just isn't firing on all cylinders. I can take that if he's doing the other side of the game a lot better than he is.
"You can see why Martin O'Neill made the substitution at half-time and there's no doubt Celtic looked much better going forward."

O'Neill admitted he sees Duran as being better through the middle, when asked about his Colombian talisman post-match, but given Hogh's price tag he might not be inclined to pull him out of the firing line just yet.
"[Duran] has played wide at his previous clubs," O'Neill said. "But I personally feel his best position is through the middle.
"It's now a matter of us trying to fit him in and I think we can do that. It's a real battle for places now."

articles.headline: The New Street Fighter Movie Gets Savaged By Critics, But Not Everyone Hates It
keyFacts: The new live-action Street Fighter movie has opened to negative reviews and a 41 percent score on Rotten Tomatoes.
Critics described the film as an incoherent mess with confusing jokes, though some praised its action sequences and entertainment value.
The movie is scheduled to release in theaters starting October 16.
body: A celebrity-filled cast. A director best known for his work on the Eric Andre show. One of the most iconic and beloved franchises in gaming. What could go wrong? Apparently quite a lot. The Street Fighter movie is getting panned by many critics. Not quite as bad as 2024’s Borderlands adaptation, but still very far from great.

Starring Noah Centineo as Ken Masters, Andrew Koji as Ryu, and Callina Liang as Chun-Li, Hollywood’s latest attempt to cash in on Capcom’s longrunning fighting game series marketed itself from the jump as a very silly affair. Cody Rhodes looks absurd as Guile. 50 Cent is playing Balrog. They even let Eric AndrÃ© on screen as ring announcer Don Sauvage. But based on early reviews, unlike Mortal Kombat 2, which committed to its dumb premise with unflinching B-action movie conviction, Street Fighter sounds like a dizzying mess of abbreviated character arcs and humor that doesn’t land.

Officially in theaters starting October 16, the live-action adaptation has opened to a 41 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. That’s even lower than A Minecraft Movie, which was completely unwatchable. Some reviews have accused director Kitao Sakurai’s take on Street Fighter of being an “incoherent, irredeemable mess” and “dumber than a box of rocks.” TheWrap slammed its 1990s nostalgia-fest as anachronistic and suffering from “cultural collapse.” The nicest thing Variety had to say about it was that the dialogue was often inaudible due to the “thundering sound mix.”

Not everyone was appalled. IndieWire applauded Street Fighter for at least not being boring, while The New York Times praised it as the sort of thing a kid who lost all their pocket change to Street Fighter in the arcade might begin to hallucinate in their dreams. Here’s what else the early reviews are saying:

[The film] overflows with convoluted plotting and confusingly engineered jokes. But a filmâs greatest sin is boring its audience, and this “Street Fighterâ should take pride in never coming close to doing that. Fans of the âStreet Fighterâ games donât spend much time thinking about the overarching lore. The games are a flashy vessel to project yourself onto while you play with martial artists, each with their own unique aesthetics. And at the end of the day, this movie delivers the same thing. Itâs a blank emotional canvas whose value lies in what you make of it â but it sure looks cool as hell. – Christian Zilko

Most importantly, the film is dedicated to the punchy pyrotechnics of its fight sequences, most of which are constructed to feature the diverse personalities of its many fighters. This can eventually seem like a weakness, as the film tries to flit between one too many showdowns, tiring viewers out while confusing them on the movieâs priorities. But in another sense, it simply feels like the natural zenith of an arcade playerâs imagination, the âand then, and thenâ output of fighter fantasies running wild. By the end, you can practically see the â90s kid smashing and kicking at the air on his way out of the theater. – Brandon Yu

David Dastmalchianâs eyes roll back as he presses his thumbs into a sniveling scientistâs eye sockets. As the skull cracks and blood splatters across Dastmalchian’s forehead, he makes an expression that can be best described as orgasm face. This happens within the first 10 minutes of Street Fighter, in which Dastmalchian plays the fighting game franchiseâs chief antagonist, M. Bison. Itâs a perfect performance â a masterclass in B-movie camp. Unfortunately, nobody else in Street Fighter is anywhere close to operating on Dastmalchianâs level. To make matters worse, not even writer-director Kitao Sakurai seems to know what kind of movie heâs making, leading to one of the sloppiest, cringiest, and most incoherent films of the year. – Jake Kleinman

Whenever Ken or Ryu start emoting or waxing philosophical like Steven Seagal or Van Damme in those movies that inspire Street Fighter, Liangâs Chun-Li calls out in the most basic terms how stupid they sound. Thereâs several knowing winks at the fans like this, guarding against criticism by owning up to how silly this all is, which would land better if the movie ever rose above the stuff itâs making fun of. Instead, Street Fighter is satisfied punching down on itself, and everything thatâs cringe about the 90s, while happily being stuck there, in the past, so it could pretend that this is as good as it gets for video game adaptations. – Radheyan Simonpillai

Street Fighter is dumber than a box of rocks, but have you ever thrown rocks at things? It can be pretty fun with the right combination of enthusiastic friends and anarchic spirit. Kitao Sakurai doesnât always succeed in marshalling his enthusiastic cast and anarchic approach to the filmâs blend of action and comedy, with too many characters there to service too thin a story, but Street Fighterâs all about landing as many punches as it can before the round timer hits zero.Â Even though there are plenty of misses, the ones it does manage to land hit hard. – Tom Jorgensen

As the film becomes increasingly split between the tournament and M. Bisonâs unraveling conspiracy, something goes terribly awry in its back half, hinting at either a troubled production, or one that was doomed from the start. The dialogue, whether expository exchanges or quippy one-liners, grows splintered, and is increasingly presented with the backs of speakersâ heads or their mouths partially obscured; it would be interesting to learn how much of the film was rewritten in post. – Siddhant Adlakha

Some fans may break out their torches and pitchforks, but I for one embrace this Frankenstein monster. Itâs so oblivious to narrative and stylistic cohesion that itâs almost spiritual. Watching âStreet Fighterâ is to exist outside time itself. Thatâs my theory and Iâm sticking to it, because otherwise thereâs no explanation for why this film begins in 1987 with Ryu listening to âWhatâs Upâ by 4 Non Blondes on his walkman, a song which wouldnât come out for another six years. When the action leaps ahead to 1993, Kenâs manager proudly declares that Taco Bell is going to name a Gordita after him, even though Taco Bell wouldnât add the Gordita to their menu until a half decade later. – William Bibbiani

“Street Fighter” is a highly watchable movie, and it’s not too hard to convince yourself you’re having fun while seeing it. Yet its aftertaste is so bitter and its center so hollow that it’s hard to recommend, and certainly not as an introduction to this world. There may be enough in the film’s attract mode to get me to press start, but I ended up not wanting to continue.” – Bill Bria

articles.headline: How to solve Notre Dame Piano puzzle in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse? War and Famine weapon location
keyFacts: Players in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse can solve the Notre Dame Organ puzzle to unlock the War and Famine weapon.
Destructoid stated that players must record random candle numbers under zodiac signs in the Stained Glass Gallery.
Players must press the organ keystrokes matching the zodiac signs in ascending candle order from one to nine.
body: Once you make your way to the Notre Dame location in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse , you’ll come across the massive Piano (or the Organ). This is tied with a secret that helps you unlock the War and Famine.
In this guide, I will provide you with an easy solution for this puzzle.
How to solve the Organ puzzle in Notre Dame in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

Screenshot and remix by Destructoid First, you need to reach the location I have marked on the image above. Here, you’ll come across a cryptic piece of text that reads as the following: Beneath these stairs lies our order’s greatest sin.
Next, head to the Stained Glass Gallery. The spot is marked on the map, so there’s no problem to access the area. If you notice the glass windows, you’ll find two interesting things.
Screenshot by Destructoid Each window has a horoscope sign on top.
Each window also has candles at its base. The number ranges between one and nine.
Take a note of two important things: the zodiac and the number of candles under each. The numbers will be completely random.

Screenshot by Destructoid Now, head back to the Zodiac Organ and start playing the notes. How do you play the notes? On the Organ, you’ll find the zodiac signs available as a keystroke. You have to press them at the exact order as the number of candles you saw.
First, step on the zodiac that has one candle. Then, step on the symbol that has two, and keep working your way up to nine. If you press a wrong key, you’ll need to start from scratch.
Once solved, follow the left of your screen, and you’ll find a secret path that will lead you to the Legendary War and Famine weapon.

articles.headline: KDE turns 30 with Plasma 6.8, remote upgrades, and an X11 farewell
keyFacts: KDE released Plasma 6.8 as its 30th Anniversary Edition on October 14, while also retiring native X11 session support in Plasma.
Legacy X11 applications will continue to function through the XWayland compatibility layer and in other desktop environments, according to KDE.
Plasma 6.8 introduces features such as Nvidia triple buffering by default, Kup backup integration, and improved window decoration support.
body: Marking the 30th anniversary of software developer KDE on October 14, the company released Plasma 6.8, debuted a movie, and retired Plasma's native X11 session support. The announcement from KDE dubs the new Plasma 6.8 as the "30th Anniversary Edition" and describes the update as preparing Plasma for the future. Legacy X11 applications will still function via the XWayland compatibility layer , and KDE applications will also continue supporting X11 under other desktop environments.

After 42 years in service, the X11 protocol is losing another major desktop environment. Plasma will fully adopt the Wayland system and put support for starting new X11 sessions in Plasma to bed. Users opting to stay on Plasma 6.7 will keep their existing sessions for now. The move was expected, with GNOME officially dropping X11 sessions by default in 2025 .

The new Plasma 6.8 brings many improvements, including increased support for adding window decorations (like shadows and rounded corners) to third-party apps, and a more streamlined Union theming system . Other notable additions include Nvidia triple buffering being enabled by default, Kup backup integration (KDE's backup utility—now integrated into Plasma), and kscreenctl , a command-line utility that allows power users to adjust display configurations.
